originality.rationale: The structural dual simplicial collapse works for every p>=2 at n>=4p+1, extending known original three-cut homology into 4p+1<=n<6p-3 for p>=5. The unrestricted 2026 primary paper proves shellability only above 6p-3; p=2,3,4 are explicitly credited. Neither total-cut results nor existing dihedral character papers cover this exact simple-homotopy statement. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent general-p dual elementary collapse may be present in unindexed literature; current published records and inspected relevant primary paper do not show it.
Published p=3 and p=4 results were compared by record statements rather than complete manuscripts; they cannot logically prove all-p coverage without an extra generalization.
The known clique-complex circle theorem is used with an independent direct short-arc nerve proof.

value.rationale: Motivated sharp threshold n>=4p+1 in current cycle-power three-cut study. The constructive dual simple-homotopy reduction explains an all-p family, obtains torsion-free integral homology for 4p+1<=n<6p-3 (a nonempty growing gap for p>=5), and naturally distinguishes previously known shellability from a strictly weaker new homology theorem. The n=4p obstruction supports boundary significance.
